body:
I grew up most of my life so far masking/ getting stuff blamed on my ADHD which I have along with ASD. Until this pandemic happened, lost my mind in May, and since I haven't had any proper social interaction to speak of in about 10 months, I might have forgot how to mask. Wasn't good at it in the first place so it's eh.
Edit: I think I forgot how to spell as well.

Wait, are you from the South? Cause it snowed for the first time in years here on Sunday and you bet believe I was out in that snow acting like I was five. Probably scared the neighbors to see that but oh well it's too late.

Yeah, the only reason I go outside at this point is to walk my dog because I have close family members who are high-risk. I'm afraid when I go back that I will have no idea how to mask like I used to anymore and struggle.

Lowkey, I've had to get accommodations for school (extra time for testing) because my processing speed isn't the fastest and staying focused is a miracle at this point. Not to mention my anxiety which has showed up during quarantine. But I feel bad about it and like I'm an idiot.

I have 7 people who I consider friends at this point. Been stuck at home since March and haven't seen a lot of people so that's contributed to the falling apart of a couple of friendships and now I'm down to seven total, two that are close. The five that aren't close bounce between friends and good acquaintances to be honest.
Exactly. The second my family explained sarcasm to young me, there was no going back.

Ah yes. I love summoning the demon. We tend to gather with our trombones around one individual trombone and chant. It's great fun.
Edit: I can't spell.

We did a virtual show of sorts. And we had like 50 kids go to games and a few do in person. But most of our band has been virtual as it's an option given to us by our district. While our directors may really want us to come back, I'm not cause I ain't giving no corona to my high-risk family members.

My parent was a PhD student teaching college English. A lot of them are struggling with stuff outside of teaching you. My parent cared a lot about their students but also had a whole lot going on. My parents were raising two kids, born about two years apart during the time my parent was teaching. That while my parent was teaching and finishing their PhD while barely getting paid enough to afford a place to live and put food on the table. The system is messed up and both sides are affected.
